### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **41** documentable anchor(s).

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c005e0e42e207b073843b255248877b84442342`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c005e0e42e207b073843b255248877b84442342` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8f1dd13aa96d90372594edd40741761f20995f92` — the merge of head `5c37471ba53aa5155b3e7fbd5cc3bc63fd547627` into base `5c005e0e42e207b073843b255248877b84442342`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8f1dd13aa96d90372594edd40741761f20995f92 && git checkout 8f1dd13aa96d90372594edd40741761f20995f92
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5c005e0e42e207b073843b255248877b84442342 5c37471ba53aa5155b3e7fbd5cc3bc63fd547627 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5c005e0e42e207b073843b255248877b84442342 && git merge --no-ff 5c37471ba53aa5155b3e7fbd5cc3bc63fd547627

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c005e0e42e207b073843b255248877b84442342
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5c005e0e42e207b073843b255248877b84442342` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5c37471ba53aa5155b3e7fbd5cc3bc63fd547627`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-disabled-holder-served-stack.test.ts, .changeset/32354-stored-rows-served-set.md (its declaration lines and level) + read as cited code, not reviewed: packages/metadata-protocol/src/served-override.ts, protocol-lock-state.ts (`declinesStoredRow`), packages/metadata-core/src/customization-pair-lookup.ts (`pairsOf`, `isPairOf`), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`packageScopedHoldersOf`, `pairRowBinding`), packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts (the four `[#32408]` pins, on `main`).

Delta review of PASS 6856157850 (on #32811, head `cd1143c1`), read at 2026-11-13T17:08Z. This PR supersedes #32811 and continues its branch with every commit kept. Inputs: the interdiff `cd1143c19..5c37471ba` (the merge of `main` `6abfd47e`, the fix commit `032a1eda` and the commit `5c37471b`), the whole diff against merge base `2c98485d` (seven files, now this card's alone), the PR body, the check-runs on this head, the knocks 6858423486 and 6858982833. Claim 6859006109. No record was posted on `032a1eda`: its `Test Core (4/8)` went red while the draft waited on the check-runs, and the head moved. Everything the earlier record judged and the interdiff does not touch stands as read there.

### ① Derived judgments

- Unchanged and right: C1a, C1b, C1c (widening), Q2 (narrowing), Q2′, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- The three moves the earlier record found unlisted are settled. The in-process layered read no longer moves in the Q2 state (S1). The disabled pair's address is declared as a narrowing (S2). Bare `/published` is in the Q2 line (S3).
- C3 is now declared as what it is: no move since 18.4.0, with a second guard added here.
- The single-holder re-addressing of the in-process layered read is stated in the changeset's second paragraph. It refuses nothing.
- S2 and the N2 rows are measured and pinned on `RestServer` only, and the changeset says so on each line.
- The last commit adds no move. It takes back two answers `032a1eda` had moved without declaring them: a row bound to a holder's customization pair was counted as a row of an enabled package of its own, so with every holder disabled the bare read served it. `main` withholds it (the `[#32408]` pins in `packages/objectql`), and so does this head. The changeset sentence now states the rule for every pair row, not only a disabled holder's declared override.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged: `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, the `!` title, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
- The BREAKING headline now names this release's two narrowings (Q2 on the plain read and `/published`; the disabled pair's address) and no longer C3. The "before" column is stated as 18.4.0.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head, all concluded: 51 runs, 35 success, 16 skipped, none failed. On `032a1eda` `Test Core (4/8)` was red on two `[#32408]` pins of `packages/objectql`; it is green here.
- The dogfood battery the `!` title owes was run on `032a1eda` (PR body). The knock for this head names the objectql file, the REST and runtime pin files and the `metadata-protocol` suite, not the battery, and the dogfood shards are skipped in this head's check-runs. The seat's.
- The merge of `main`: two conflicts, both on #32808's own hunks. The `getMetaItemLayered` host list is the union; `meta-legacy-pair-served.test.ts` is `main`'s copy; the consumed `.changeset/32501-…` is not re-added. The diff against `main` is seven files, none of #32501's.
- `main` is seven commits past the merge base, none on a path of this diff.
- `Part of #32354`: the list cases of epic note 6820147040 stay on the card. Routing them is the seat's, before ACCEPT.
- Epic red-line read: owed from the epic seat before ACCEPT. Not this record's.
- N3 of the earlier record (the bare read reads the active rows twice while a package is disabled) is left as it was: accepted as a deviation.
- The ablation legs in the PR body and in the knock are the report's; none was run here.
- The PR body, as read at 16:39Z, still describes `032a1eda`: hunk 1 names the old exclusion (`isServedOverrideRowOf`), and Verification is "all on head `032a1edad8`". Its local runs covered `metadata-protocol`, `rest`, `runtime` and the dogfood battery, not `packages/objectql`, where the two pins went red. The seat's at ACCEPT.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts`. `servedAddressJudgment` answers the judgment and never throws; only the plain read turns a refusal into a throw (`servedAddressOf`). The rows are read once and judged twice: all of them decide whether a disabled package holds the name and whether a package-less row leaves the read alone, and only the rows the reads serve name a served holder (S4). A row bound to a customization pair of any holder of the name names no holder either (N2, widened by `5c37471b`): the pair is asked with `pairsOf` of each holder the registry reads, disabled ones included, which is the lookup the registry's own pair-row binding asks (`isPairOf`). So an enabled holder's pair row no longer makes the pair a second holder, and a disabled holder's pair row is withheld with it, declared override or not. A pair whose row sits beside no holder it is a pair of still holds the name as a package of its own, which is S2's reading. The declined-row exclusion is the read's own predicate, as before. The member selector is resolved once, as the layered read resolves it (N1).

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts`, `protocol.ts` (S1). Fixed, by the first of the two ways the earlier record offered. `getMetaItemLayered` re-addresses on one served holder and otherwise reads as it did, so the security catalog echo and the lock gate keep their answer in the Q2 state. `packagelessLayeredReadRefusal` returns the served-holders refusal to the door, as its signature says, and the docblock now states both. Pinned: in the Q2 state the in-process read resolves and the door's refusal names only the enabled holders.

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts` (S2). The code is as reviewed. The move is now declared and pinned with and without the pair's override row, with the enabled pair as CONTROL and the base's own address unmoved.

`.changeset/32354-stored-rows-served-set.md` (S3, as declarations). Fixed as asked.

`packages/rest/src/meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-disabled-holder-served-stack.test.ts`. The new pins state the rule each finding named and nothing else. Bare `/published` in the Q2 state is pinned on both transports.

Findings:

- **n1 nit.** The docblock above the pair describe in `meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts` says the answers were measured the same on `main`, "so neither case moves", and that with no row the pair's address is refused. The pins under it, the PR's MAIN leg (S2 red twice, N2 beside E red once) and the changeset say the opposite: S2 moves 200 → 404, and the enabled pair's address with no row serves the base's item. The comment is from an earlier fix round; correct it on any next push.
- **n2 nit.** `pairRow` asks the holders the registry reads (`every`). A package that holds the name only through a stored row that lost the bare slot is in `rows.candidates` and not in `every`, so a row at its pair would still be counted for the pair. Derived, not run, and not shown reachable (it takes a pair row beside a base that holds the name only as a row, and a third row); the guard on `032a1eda` had the same reach. Asking `rows.candidates` as well is one spread.

No must-fix and no should-fix. S1 to S4, N1 and N2 of record 6856157850 are closed on this head.
